sections.h2: Where to pay and who sets the bill
sections.html:
From December 1 through May 31 the Town of Brookhaven's Receiver of Taxes collects the bill. After that, the Suffolk County Comptroller takes over. The tax office is in Town Hall at 1 Independence Hill in Farmingville, 631-451-9009, and the Assessor works in the same building. The town stretches from Port Jefferson and Stony Brook on the North Shore to Patchogue on the South Shore, with a 2020 population of 485,773, so one office serves areas with very different school districts and home prices.

The Receiver collects and does not set rates. School budgets come from your school district, the county levy from the county budget, and the town levy from the Supervisor and Town Board.

sections.h2: Tax year and when bills arrive
sections.html:
Town, county and school taxes in Suffolk County run from December 1 through the following November 30. The bill becomes a lien on December 1, and the town mails it in mid-December. You should have it by December 15. If it has not come by the third week of December, call the tax office.

The online tax system shuts on June 1 for the tax year that just ended and reopens when the next season starts in December. Owners with a mortgage escrow account get an informational bill around mid-July, while the lender gets the payment copy directly.

The first half is due January 10 and the second half May 31. The town accepts one bill split into two payments. After the first-half date, interest steps up each month, and May 31 is the last day to pay without going delinquent.

Payment madeInterest added on the first half
January 11 to February 101%
February 11 to March 102%
March 11 to April 103%
April 11 to May 104%
May 11 to May 315%

Owners who receive Enhanced STAR or the over-65 exemption get five more business days after May 31. Past that date the account is delinquent and payable to the Suffolk County Comptroller, who adds a 5 percent penalty plus interest of 1 percent per month counted from February 1. The town plays no part in the delinquency process.

You can pay online, in person or by mail, but postmarks matter. A federal change that took effect December 24, 2025 means mail dropped in a box may not get a same-day postmark. A hand-stamped envelope from a post office counter is the only method the town can guarantee, and the tax office cannot waive penalties when a payment lacks a timely postmark.

  • Online: an e-check costs $1.75 and a credit card carries a 2.35 percent fee. Partial payments cannot be made online.
  • Drop box: outside the front lobby of Town Hall, open around the clock, no cash accepted. A receipt is mailed the next business day.
  • Walk-in: Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Mail: send the right stub with the check, postmarked by January 10 for the first half and May 31 for the second half.

The Receiver and the Comptroller both accept partial payments of $200 or more plus any interest. A returned check adds a $20 charge.

File between May 1 and Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. The next one is Tuesday, May 18, 2027. An online application opens May 1 and closes at the end of Grievance Day. March 1 is the taxable status date, which is also when exemption applications are due. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the final roll July 1.

A paper grievance goes to the Town of Brookhaven Assessor, Attention: Grievance, at 1 Independence Hill, or into the Assessor's bin at the main lobby security desk. Hearings are held at Town Hall on Grievance Day, and the Assessor sometimes adds evening and weekend hours beforehand, so check the Grievance Day page each spring for the schedule.

Late filers get nothing. Applications submitted before May 1 or after the Grievance Day deadline are returned to the applicant.

Suffolk County law makes paying on time the owner's duty even when no bill arrived, and the owner owes the penalties and interest for a late payment. Since bills go out in December, buyers in Suffolk County are told to call the Receiver and confirm every tax is current.

  • Ask the Receiver for a current figure and note whether the first half or the whole year is paid
  • If the bill went to a former address, give the Receiver the right mailing address
  • After May 31, ask the Suffolk County Comptroller for the payoff. The check address is 330 Center Drive in Riverhead.

Taxes still unpaid at the tax lien sale, which usually happens in December, lead the Comptroller to sell a lien to Suffolk County. A cash buyer can pay off a delinquent balance at closing the same way a lender would, which avoids that sale.

Brookhaven is mostly owner-occupied. About 80.9 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. The estimated population in July 2025 was 496,410, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $489,200 and median gross rent is $2,314. The Long Island Rail Road serves the area. If your valuation looks out of line with similar houses nearby, call the Assessor before May.

sections.h2: Closing steps for a cash sale
sections.html:
With cash, the schedule is set by title work and the payoff figures. A short sequence keeps it moving:

  1. Get the current balance from the Receiver, or from the Comptroller after May 31.
  2. Confirm your mailing address is right so no bill goes astray.
  3. Give the figures to your closing attorney or title agent.
  4. Review the closing statement and make sure the tax line matches the number you were given.

Because the payoff comes out of your proceeds, you do not bring money to the table. Ask whether the first half, the second half or the whole year has been paid so the buyer's credit is calculated correctly.

faqs.q: When are Brookhaven property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by January 10 and the second half by May 31. Late first-half payments add 1 percent for each month, up to 5 percent in the last three weeks of May.

faqs.q: Who do I pay after May 31 in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Comptroller, at the Suffolk County Treasurer address on Center Drive in Riverhead. A 5 percent penalty plus 1 percent a month from February 1 is added to the balance.

faqs.q: Can I pay Brookhaven tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, online, with a 2.35 percent bank fee. An e-check costs $1.75. Neither fee goes to the town, and partial payments cannot be made online.
The third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. Applications are accepted from May 1 through that day.

faqs.q: What if I never got a Brookhaven tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax and any penalties. Call the Receiver of Taxes at 631-451-9009 if the bill has not arrived by the third week of December, and keep your mailing address current.
